forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Hams faces £394,000 budget gap for 2027/28 despite identifying £2m in savings
news_drafts.lead: South Hams District Council identified £2.071m in savings and cost reductions for 2027/28 but still faces a shortfall of £394,542, according to its medium-term financial strategy approved at the executive meeting on 16 September. The gap represents 2.6 per cent of the council's projected net budget of £15.152m. Larger deficits are forecast for the following two years: £1.455m in 2028/29 and £1.165m in 2029/30. The council's earmarked reserves are being depleted rapidly to fund capital projects and to cover two major contractor failures — a waste service collapse that cost £4m to bring back in-house, and the administration of leisure contractor Fusion, which required £1.2m to restore services. The council's reserves are projected to fall from £13.957m to £6.731m by March 2028. Government funding cuts have compounded the pressure: the Revenue Support Grant falls from £3.7m to £1.8m over three years, and a business rates reset eliminated £2.5m of income.

findings.headline: Local Plan team and Planning Policy salary costs are being funded from reserves rather than operating budgets, with Local Plan withdrawals jumping to £290,000 in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The council is withdrawing from reserves to cover salary costs: Planning Policy and Major Developments drew £98,000 in 2025/26 for salaries; the Local Plan team salary funding increased from £80,000 in 2025/26 to £290,000 in 2026/27. This pattern suggests operating budgets may not be fully covering these service salaries and the council is relying on reserve drawdown.
findings.matters: Funding operational salary costs from reserves rather than recurrent budgets is a sign of structural budget pressure and raises questions about the council's underlying budget sustainability.
findings.figures: Planning Policy salaries: £98,000 (2025/26); Local Plan salaries: £80,000 (2025/26) and £290,000 (2026/27)
findings.quote: Local Plan (to part fund salaries of the Local Plan team)

findings.headline: Reserve withdrawals from Business Rates Retention Reserve increase to £500,000 in 2027/28, up from £300,000 in earlier years.
findings.detail: The council is drawing down the Business Rates Retention Reserve more heavily in the outer year. Total withdrawals across all reserves also rise from £380,000 in 2026/27 to £790,000 in 2027/28—more than double. This increasing reliance on reserves occurs at the same time that NHB funding is being lost.
findings.matters: A lender would need to understand whether these rising drawdowns reflect planned depletion of reserves to fund specific items, or whether they signal structural budget pressure that reserves are being used to bridge.
findings.figures: £500,000 (2027/28 BRRR withdrawal); total reserves drawn: £380,000 (2026/27) increasing to £790,000 (2027/28)

findings.headline: New Homes Bonus scheme ends after 2025/26, eliminating a funding stream and reducing total reserve contributions by £686,300 in 2027/28.
findings.detail: The council receives New Homes Bonus funding of £530,422 in 2025/26, but the scheme terminates after that year. Total contributions to earmarked reserves decline from £1,248,300 in 2026/27 to £562,000 in 2027/28—a reduction of £686,300. This swing reflects both the loss of NHB and the council's adjustment to a smaller future reserve position.
findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's financial sustainability needs to understand how it will absorb the loss of £530k+ in recurring funding and whether operating budgets are configured to function without it.
findings.quote: (2025/26 is the last year of the NHB scheme)
